title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Open-Source AI Leadership Act seeks to position the United States as a global frontrunner in artificial intelligence by encouraging the development and widespread use of open‑source AI technologies. It aims to provide funding, support research, and forge public‑private partnerships that promote transparency, collaboration, and innovation across the AI ecosystem.

title: To amend the National Institute of Standards and Technology Act to authorize certain assessments by the Director of the Institute and impose requirements on certain memorandums of understanding relating to artificial intelligence, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: This amendment allows the NIST Director to conduct specific assessments concerning artificial intelligence. It also establishes rules for any agreements with other parties that involve AI, along with other related provisions.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: This act is designed to shield families from the rising energy costs associated with large AI data centers. It would require data center operators to take measures—such as enforcing energy‑efficiency standards, capping their energy use, or compensating households—to limit the impact on household electricity bills.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act is a law that temporarily bans the construction and operation of new data centers dedicated to artificial intelligence. It aims to address environmental concerns, reduce carbon emissions, and encourage more sustainable computing practices.

title: LIFT AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 34 - 1.
summary: The LIFT AI Act is a proposed piece of legislation aimed at setting clear rules for how artificial intelligence is developed and used. It seeks to balance encouraging innovation with safeguards for privacy, accountability, and public trust in AI systems.

title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Children’s Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026 establishes safety standards for AI‑powered toys that children can play with, requiring manufacturers to ensure these products are free from harmful content, privacy risks, and other vulnerabilities. It imposes testing, labeling, and reporting obligations and sets penalties for non‑compliance to protect children from potential risks associated with AI in play.

title: Youth AI Privacy Act
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Youth AI Privacy Act seeks to protect the personal data of minors who use artificial‑intelligence services. It sets strict limits on data collection, storage, and sharing, requiring parental or guardian consent and ensuring that young users’ privacy is safeguarded.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires Chinese companies and research institutions to submit regular reports detailing how they develop, deploy, and manage AI technologies. This act creates a framework for transparency and oversight, ensuring that AI developments align with national policy goals and safety standards.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act establishes a national framework to advance artificial intelligence capabilities and set regulatory standards. It aims to coordinate government funding, research initiatives, and oversight to ensure AI development aligns with national interests and security objectives.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act sets out rules for how AI systems are designed, tested, and used, aiming to make them safe, fair, and trustworthy. It requires developers to assess risks, share transparency reports, and gives regulators the power to enforce penalties if those standards aren’t met.

title: A bill to provide for the delivery of artificial intelligence functional bills of materials, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Armed Services.
summary: This bill aims to establish requirements for the delivery of functional bills of materials for AI systems, ensuring transparency and accountability in AI development. It also includes additional provisions related to other aspects of AI policy and regulation.

title: Workforce for AI Trust Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Workforce for AI Trust Act aims to develop a skilled workforce to support safe and trustworthy AI development. It proposes training, education, and employment initiatives to ensure the industry has the expertise needed to build reliable AI systems.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 establishes rules to reduce the environmental footprint of AI systems, requiring companies to meet energy‑efficiency standards and report on the carbon emissions of their AI infrastructure. It also creates oversight and incentive programs to encourage responsible hardware lifecycle management and the adoption of greener AI practices.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This act seeks to stop AI firms from exploiting consumers with inflated pricing and from manipulating labor markets to fix wages at unfair levels. It introduces regulations and penalties to enforce reasonable AI service costs and protect workers from wage suppression.

title: FARM AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Agriculture.
summary: The FARM AI Act of 2026 is a U.S. law designed to govern the use of artificial intelligence in agriculture, aiming to promote safe, transparent, and responsible AI practices on farms. It establishes standards for data privacy, accountability, and oversight to protect farmers, consumers, and the environment while encouraging innovation in precision agriculture.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
summary: The Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act aims to encourage the development and deployment of AI technologies in banking and finance. It provides a framework for regulation, risk assessment, and ethical standards to ensure innovation while protecting consumers and maintaining financial stability.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 619.
summary: The Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act is a legislative effort designed to stimulate the development and deployment of artificial intelligence technologies within the banking and finance sector. It sets out regulatory frameworks, incentives, and safeguards to balance innovation with consumer protection and market stability.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act is a proposed law designed to strengthen the United States’ position in AI by cultivating a highly skilled workforce. It aims to create programs, incentives, and partnerships that train, attract, and retain talent in AI and related innovation fields.

title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
summary: The No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act bars the creation of artificial‑intelligence data centers on lands owned by the federal government. This law seeks to protect federal resources and prevent AI infrastructure from operating within federally controlled territories.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 requires schools to integrate AI education into the curriculum, ensuring students understand how AI works, its benefits, and its risks. The law also provides funding and resources for teacher training, classroom materials, and safe, ethical use of AI tools in schools.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 aims to equip students and educators with the skills and knowledge needed to safely and responsibly use artificial intelligence tools in schools. It proposes nationwide standards, teacher training programs, and curriculum updates that encourage critical thinking about AI’s benefits and risks while ensuring equitable access for all students.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed law that aims to set clear rules for how artificial intelligence systems are developed and used. It focuses on ensuring AI is built safely and transparently, holding creators accountable while still encouraging innovation.

title: Understanding AI in the Classroom Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The “Understanding AI in the Classroom Act” aims to clarify how artificial intelligence tools are used in schools, ensuring they are integrated safely and responsibly. It likely establishes guidelines for teachers, students, and administrators to navigate AI’s benefits and risks while fostering informed digital literacy.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that every American and community impacted by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center should have the right to transparency and local autonomy.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy states that every American and community affected by the construction or operation of an AI data center should have the right to understand what’s happening and to participate in decisions that affect them. It emphasizes the importance of transparency and local control so residents can be informed and have a say in how these data centers are built and run.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 is designed to ensure that AI technologies used in veterans' services are safe, ethical, and transparent. It establishes guidelines, oversight, and funding to protect veterans’ well‑being and uphold their rights when AI is integrated into healthcare, benefits, and support programs.

title: Safeguarding Against Fabricated Exploitation Through Artificial Intelligence Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The “Safeguarding Against Fabricated Exploitation Through Artificial Intelligence Act of 2026” establishes legal safeguards to prevent AI systems from generating or spreading false or harmful content that could deceive or exploit individuals. It requires AI developers to implement transparency, accountability, and robust verification measures so that such fabricated exploitation can be detected and mitigated.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 requires federal agencies to study how artificial intelligence tools are used in judicial proceedings and to report those findings to Congress. It creates an independent oversight council that reviews AI applications for fairness, accuracy, and privacy before they can be adopted in courts.

title: A bill to require a report on the use of artificial intelligence with respect to access to unminimized information collected pursuant to the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: This bill would require a report that explains how artificial intelligence is used to access unminimized information gathered under the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. It also covers additional related purposes beyond that reporting requirement.
